newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Samsung wins Kazakh copper plant sale - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Samsung wins Kazakh copper plant sale - Interfax.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Co Ltd has won a tender for the right to buy the assets of Kazakhstan's Balkhasmys copper plant, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

It quoted Eduard Utepov, in charge of Kazakhstan's privatisation, as saying that under the tender, which was not publicly announced, Samsung would invest around $700 million between 1997 and 2000 in modernising metal production at the plant and developing its mining base.
Interfax said $80 million would be invested this year.

The tender apparently annuls a September 1996 sale of the major copper plant to a consortium grouping Glencore AG of Switzerland, Phelps Dodge Corp of the United States and Kazkommerzbank, a Kazakh commercial bank.
Kazakh officials were not available for comment.
Interfax said the South Korean firm planned to boost copper production to 200,000 tonnes by 2000, adding that output in 1996 was 80,000 tonnes, well down on 1995 output of around 135,000 tonnes.
